duas.who: King Saul and the believers with him
the believers of the Children of Israel

q: When Ibraheem ﵊ said, “O my Rabb! Make this
and feed with fruit those inhabitants who believe in Allaah and the Last Day.”

(Allaah accepted this prayer and made Makkah a place where no killing should take place, no plants should be uprooted and no animal hunted. Allaah also saw to it that Makkah receives food and products from the entire world.)
Allaah said, “As for him who carries out kufr, I shall grant him enjoyment for a while, after which I will drive
him into the punishment of the Fire
It is the worst of places to be.”
2:126.s: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day." [God] said, "And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."
2:126.c: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this city ˹of Mecca˺ secure and provide fruits to its people—those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.” He answered, “As for those who disbelieve, I will let them enjoy themselves for a little while, then I will condemn them to the torment of the Fire. What an evil destination!”

q: When Ibraheem ﵊ and Ismaa'eel ﵊ were raising the foundation of the House
Indeed You are the All Hearing, the All Knowing
(You hear our prayer and know our intentions and actions).”
2:127.s: And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], "Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.
2:127.c: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham raised the foundation of the House with Ishmael, ˹both praying,˺ “Our Lord! Accept ˹this˺ from us. You are indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

q: “O our Rabb! Make us obedient to You and make from our descendants
that is also obedient to You. Show us
(the manner in which we should worship You)
Without doubt, You are the Most Pardoning, the Most Merciful.”
(Although they were sinless, they asked for forgiveness because they were humble and this was done to teach people to ask for forgiveness after every good act.)
2:128.s: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites [of hajj and ‘umrah] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
2:128.c: Our Lord! Make us both ˹fully˺ submit to You and from our descendants a nation that will submit to you. Show us our rituals, and turn to us in grace. You are truly the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

q: to them, teach them the Book
(the meanings and necessary explanations of the Qur'aan)
(the Sunnat and the hidden mysteries and intricate allegories of the Qur'aan)
Without doubt, You are the Mighty, the Wise.”
2:129.s: Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
2:129.c: Our Lord! Raise from among them a messenger who will recite to them Your revelations, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Indeed, You ˹alone˺ are the Almighty, All-Wise.”

q: (when he left his wife Haajira and son Isma'eel in Makkah),
“O my Rabb! Make this city peaceful and safeguard my children and myself from worshipping idols.”
(Allaah accepted his du'aa by declaring Makkah a sacred place where no person should be killed.)
14:35.s: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this city [i.e., Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.
14:35.c: ˹Remember˺ when Abraham prayed, “My Lord! Make this city ˹of Mecca˺ secure, and keep me and my children away from the worship of idols.

q: “O my Rabb! Indeed these idols have misled many people. So whoever will follow me
then he is certainly from me
(from among the followers of my religion).
And whoever will disobey me, then
(I pray that you give him the ability to obey me because)
surely You are Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
14:36.s: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me - then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are [yet] Forgiving and Merciful.
14:36.c: My Lord! They have caused many people to go astray. So whoever follows me is with me, and whoever disobeys me—then surely You are ˹still˺ All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: “O our Rabb! I have settled some of my children
in a valley that cannot be cultivated, close to Your sacred house
So that they establish salaah, so cause
the hearts of some people to be inclined towards them
(so that people may love them and settle with them).
for their sustenance so that they may be grateful.”

(As a result of this du'aa, despite being a place where crops do not generally grow, Makkah receives food and manufactured articles from all over the world, especially from Taa'if, apiece of fertile land which Allaah took from Shaam and placed next to Makkah.)
14:37.s: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
14:37.c: Our Lord! I have settled some of my offspring in a barren valley, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of ˹believing˺ people incline towards them and provide them with fruits, so perhaps they will be thankful.

q: “O our Rabb! Indeed You know what we conceal and what we disclose
(so forgive us for all the mistakes we make).
Nothing in the heavens and the earth is hidden from Allaah.”
14:38.s: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from God on the earth or in the heaven.
14:38.c: Our Lord! You certainly know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah.

q: “All praise be to Allaah, Who has gifted
old age. Undoubtedly, my Rabb hears all prayers.”
14:39.s: Praise to God, who has granted to me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
14:39.c: All praise is for Allah who has blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Lord is indeed the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.

q: “O my Rabb! Make me one who establishes salaah, and my progeny as well. O my Rabb! Accept my prayer.”
14:40.s: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
14:40.c: My Lord! Make me and those ˹believers˺ of my descendants keep up prayer. Our Lord! Accept my prayers.

q: “O our Rabb! Forgive me, my parents and the Mu'mineen on the day when reckoning shall commence
14:41.s: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established."
14:41.c: Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the judgment will come to pass.”

q: “O my Rabb! Grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous
26:83.s: [And he said], "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous.
26:83.c: “My Lord! Grant me wisdom, and join me with the righteous.

q: “Maintain a favourable word for me among those who are to come
(let all the people who are to come after me speak only good of me).'
26:84.s: And grant me a mention [i.e., reputation] of honour among later generations.
26:84.c: Bless me with honourable mention among later generations.

q: “And make me from the inheritors of the bounteous Jannah
26:85.s: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure.
26:85.c: Make me one of those awarded the Garden of Bliss.

q: “Forgive my father, for he is among those who have gone astray.”
(Ibraheem ﵊ made this du'aa with the hope that Allaah will guide his father to accept Imaan. Once a person has died as a Kaafir, it is not permissible to make du'aa asking forgiveness for him/her.)
26:86.s: And forgive my father. Indeed, he has been of those astray.
26:86.c: Forgive my father, for he is certainly one of the misguided.

q: “Do not disgrace me on the Day
26:87.s: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are [all] resurrected -
26:87.c: And do not disgrace me on the Day all will be resurrected—

q: “...the day when neither wealth nor sons will be of any benefit
(will be unable to save anyone from punishment)...”
26:88.s: The Day when there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children
26:88.c: the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.

q: (that these will be a source of benefit)
for him who comes to Allaah with a sound
(a heart free of Shirk).” (The wealth and children of such a person can benefit him because he would have used these in Allaah's obedience, thereby earning reward for this in the Aakhirah).
26:89.s: But only one who comes to God with a sound heart."
26:89.c: Only those who come before Allah with a pure heart ˹will be saved˺.”

q: They both said, “O our Rabb! We have oppressed our souls
and if You do not forgive us and show mercy to us, we will surely be of the losers
7:23.s: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
7:23.c: They replied, “Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will certainly be losers.”

q: Isa the son of Maryam prayed, “O Allaah, our Rabb! Send down to us a set table
from the heavens so that it may be a
celebration for those of us present here and for those of us still to come
show Your power and prove the truthfulness of my Prophethood).
Provide for us, for You are the Best of providers
(because You can provide without effort or labour).”
5:114.s: Said Jesus, the son of Mary, "O God, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers."
5:114.c: Jesus, son of Mary, prayed, “O Allah, our Lord! Send us from heaven a table spread with food as a feast for us—the first and last of us—and as a sign from You. Provide for us! You are indeed the Best Provider.”

q: when Ayyoob ﵊ prayed to his Rabb
(when he lost his wealth and children and was afflicted with a disease)
saying, “Difficulty has certainly afflicted me and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy
(so remove my difficulty by Your mercy).”
21:83.s: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."
21:83.c: And ˹remember˺ when Job cried out to his Lord, “I have been touched with adversity, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”

q: and thought that We would not straiten
(However, when a large fish swallowed him),
saying, “There is no Ilaah but You
You are Pure. I have certainly been from among the wrongdoers
(so please forgive me and remove me from this fish).”
21:87.s: And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."
21:87.c: And ˹remember˺ when the Man of the Whale stormed off ˹from his city˺ in a rage, thinking We would not restrain him. Then in the ˹veils of˺ darkness he cried out, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong.”

q: Yusuf ﵊ prayed, “O my Rabb! The prison is dearer to me than that
towards which these women call me. If You do not turn their plot away from me, I
(fear that as a human being, I)
may incline towards them and become of the ignorant
12:33.s: He said, "My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."
12:33.c: Joseph prayed, “My Lord! I would rather be in jail than do what they invite me to. And if You do not turn their cunning away from me, I might yield to them and fall into ignorance.”

q: (Towards the end of his life, Yusuf ﵊ prayed,)

“O my Rabb! Indeed You have granted me a part of kingship and taught me the interpretation of dreams. O Creator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Protecting Friend in this world and in the Aakhirah. Grant me death in a state of obedience
and include me among Your pious bondsmen
12:101.s: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”
12:101.c: “My Lord! You have surely granted me authority and taught me the interpretation of dreams. ˹O˺ Originator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter. Allow me to die as one who submits and join me with the righteous.” Reminders to Prophet Muḥammad

q: Moosa ﵊ said, “O our Rabb! Indeed you have granted splendour
and wealth to Fir'oun and his ministers in this worldly life. O our Rabb! This
O our Rabb! Destroy their wealth
(so that they cannot use it for evil purposes)
and harden their hearts so that they do not have Imaan until they witness a painful punishment
(a time when having Imaan will be futile since it will there be too late).” (Haaroon ﵊ also joined Moosa ﵊ in this du'aa by saying “Aameen”.)
10:88.s: And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead [men] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."
10:88.c: Moses prayed, “Our Lord! You have granted Pharaoh and his chiefs luxuries and riches in this worldly life, ˹which they abused˺ to lead people astray from Your Way! Our Lord, destroy their riches and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.”

q: said, “The prayer that the two of you have made has been accepted. So remain upright
and never follow the path of those without knowledge.”
(Do not follow those who fail to understand that We have sound reasons for not punishing people immediately.)
10:89.s: [God] said, "Your supplication has been answered." So remain on a right course and follow not the way of those who do not know."
10:89.c: Allah responded ˹to Moses and Aaron˺, “Your prayer is answered! So be steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”

q: (Realising that the task was a great one,)
(to be able to bear Your message and to have the courage to propagate it)...”
20:25.s: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]
20:25.c: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Uplift my heart for me,

20:26.s: And ease for me my task

20:27.s: And untie the knot from my tongue
20:27.c: and remove the impediment from my tongue

20:28.s: That they may understand my speech.
20:28.c: so people may understand my speech,

20:29.s: And appoint for me a minister [i.e., assistant] from my family -
20:29.c: and grant me a helper from my family,

q: “...and make him a partner to my task
20:32.s: And let him share my task
20:32.c: and let him share my task,

20:33.s: That we may exalt You much
20:33.c: so that we may glorify You much

q: (because it is easier to achieve something when the responsibility is shared).”
“Undoubtedly You are Ever Watchful over us
20:35.s: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."
20:35.c: for truly You have ˹always˺ been overseeing us.”

q: (When making Hijrah to Madinah, Rasulullaah ﷺ was commanded to)
Say, “O my Rabb! Allow me to enter a pleasant
pleasantly and grant me such authority from Yourself that is coupled with
(so that I may be able to overcome all my enemies).'
17:80.s: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
17:80.c: And say, “My Lord! Grant me an honourable entrance and an honourable exit and give me a supporting authority from Yourself.”

q: Exalted is Allaah, the True King.
Do not be hasty with the Qur'aan
(do not try to repeat the verses of the Qur'aan)
before its revelation is completed to you
(wait for Jibra'eel ﵊ to recite the complete verses to you before attempting to repeat them).
(praying to Allaah to allow you to remember all of it,)
say “O my Rabb! Increase my knowledge.”
20:114.s: So high [above all] is God, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
20:114.c: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran ˹O Prophet˺ before it is ˹properly˺ conveyed to you, and pray, “My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.”

q: (After preaching to his people for 950 years without a favour able response from them)
Nooh ﵊ said, “O my Rabb! Assist me
23:26.s: [Noah] said, "My Lord, support me because they have denied me."
23:26.c: Noah prayed, “My Lord! Help me, because they have denied ˹me˺.”

q: (Finally, after preaching to them for 950 years)
said, “O my Rabb! My people have rejected me
26:117.s: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.
26:117.c: Noah prayed, “My Lord! My people have truly rejected me.

q: and rescue me and those Mu'mineen who are with me.”
26:118.s: Then judge between me and them with decisive judgement and save me and those with me of the believers."
26:118.c: So judge between me and them decisively, and save me and the believers with me.”

q: and said that he was a madman and he was rebuked
54:9.s: The people of Noah denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled.
54:9.c: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺ and rejected Our servant, calling ˹him˺ insane. And he was intimidated.

q: So he made du'aa to his Rabb
“Indeed I am overpowered so assist me
(avenge my cause and destroy them, leaving no Kaafir alive).'
54:10.s: So he invoked his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help."
54:10.c: So he cried out to his Lord, “I am helpless, so help ˹me˺!”

q: Nooh ﵊ said, “O my Rabb! Do not leave even one of the Kaafiroon
71:26.s: And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.
71:26.c: Noah had prayed, “My Lord! Do not leave a single disbeliever on earth.

q: “O my Rabb! Forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my home as a Mu'min and all the Mu'mineen and Mu'minaat.
(As for the Kuffaar, I pray that you)
(Do not let any of them survive.)

Surah Nooh quoted graphically the experience of Nooh that Allaah is the Only fountain head of all blessings. Surah Jinn now presents similar proofs from the statements of the Mu'mineen Jinn to prove this belief. People are informed in this Surah that even the Jinn listen to the Qur'aan and preach Towheed to their species.
71:28.s: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction."
71:28.c: My Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house in faith, and ˹all˺ believing men and women. And increase the wrongdoers only in destruction.”

q: said, “O my Rabb! Forgive me and grant
me a kingdom that cannot be had by any other after me. Undoubtedly, You are the Great Giver.”
38:35.s: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
38:35.c: He prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me, and grant me an authority that will never be matched by anyone after me. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.”

q: “We would surely be forging a lie against Allaah if we were to return to your religion after Allaah had rescued us from it
(because this would mean that Allaah prefers us to follow your false religion).
except if our Rabb Allaah wills.
(It is a different matter if Allaah had predestined that we should return to your religion for reasons He knows best.)
The knowledge of our Rabb surrounds
everything and in Him alone do we trust
(we trust that Allaah will keep us steadfast on His true Deen and not cause us to deviate). (However, when Shu'ayb ﵊ realised that his people would not listen to him, he prayed)
O our Rabb! Decide between us and our people with the truth, for You are the best of deciders
(let it be known who is on the right and who is not).”
7:89.s: We would have invented against God a lie if we returned to your religion after God had saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that God, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon God we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision."
7:89.c: We would surely be fabricating a lie against Allah if we were to return to your faith after Allah has saved us from it. It does not befit us to return to it unless it is the Will of Allah, our Lord. Our Lord has encompassed everything in ˹His˺ knowledge. In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Judge between us and our people with truth. You are the best of those who judge.”

q: (when it occurred to him that just as Allaah can supply Maryam with fruit that are out of season, He can give children to Zakariyya ﵊ and his wife even though they had passed the age of bearing children)
Zakariyya ﵊ prayed to his Rabb saying, “My Rabb, grant me pure
Without doubt You hear all prayers
3:38.s: At that, Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
3:38.c: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”

q: Mention of the mercy of your Rabb towards His slave
19:2.s: [This is] a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
19:2.c: ˹This is˺ a reminder of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zachariah,

19:3.s: When he called to his Lord a private call [i.e., supplication].
19:3.c: when he cried out to his Lord privately,

q: “O my Rabb! My bones have weakened
and my hair has turned white because of old age. I have never
(I therefore have great hope that this du'aa will also be accepted).'
19:4.s: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy [i.e., disappointed].
19:4.c: saying, “My Lord! Surely my bones have become brittle, and grey hair has spread across my head, but I have never been disappointed in my prayer to You, my Lord!

q: “I fear for my relatives after me
(I fear that they may forsake the Deen after I die).
(a son to help me in propagating the Deen)...”
19:5.s: And indeed, I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir
19:5.c: And I am concerned about ˹the faith of˺ my relatives after me, since my wife is barren. So grant me, by Your grace, an heir,

q: from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qoob
(so that he can guide my people if they stray from their Deen).
And, O my Rabb, make him beloved unto You
(by making him a person who practises the knowledge of Deen that he possesses).'
19:6.s: Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]."
19:6.c: who will inherit ˹prophethood˺ from me and the family of Jacob, and make him, O Lord, pleasing ˹to You˺!”

q: “O my Rabb! Do not leave me childless when You are the Best
21:89.s: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors."
21:89.c: And ˹remember˺ when Zachariah cried out to his Lord, “My Lord! Do not leave me childless, though You are the Best of Successors.”

q: So We responded to his du'aa, gifted him with
(allowed her to bear children in her old age).
hasten to perform good deeds and prayed to Us in anticipation(
21:90.s: So We responded to him, and We gave to him John, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.
21:90.c: So We answered his prayer, granted him John, and made his wife fertile. Indeed, they used to race in doing good, and call upon Us with hope and fear, totally humbling themselves before Us.

q: “O our Rabb! Admit them into the Jannaat of eternity, which You have promised them, as well as the righteous ones from among their fathers, their spouses, and their progeny
(allow them all to live together in Jannah as they did in the world).
Undoubtedly, You are the Mighty, the Wise.”
40:8.s: Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
40:8.c: Our Lord! Admit them into the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them, along with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants. You ˹alone˺ are truly the Almighty, All-Wise.

q: You have certainly showered Your mercy on the one whom You have saved from difficulties on that day
This is indeed the greatest success.”
40:9.s: And protect them from the evil consequences [of their deeds]. And he whom You protect from evil consequences that Day - You will have given him mercy. And that is the great attainment."
40:9.c: And protect them from ˹the consequences of their˺ evil deeds. For whoever You protect from the evil of their deeds on that Day will have been shown Your mercy. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.”

q: (Hanna bint Faqudha conceived a child and)
said, “O my Rabb, I vow to You
is in my belly to be free
(from all worldly duties and dedicated only to Your service),
from me. Verily only You are The All Seeing, The All Knowing
3:35.s: [Mention, O Muhammad], when the wife of ‘Imrān said, “My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”
3:35.c: ˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said, “My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service, so accept it from me. You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”

q: When she delivered the child, she said
“My Rabb, I have delivered a girl”
Allaah knows best what she delivered
(He knew best the value of the baby girl).
Male and female are not alike.
“I shall name her Maryam and I seek Your protection for her and for her offspring from the accursed Shaytaan.”
3:36.s: But when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And God was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. "And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of God]."
3:36.c: When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a girl,”—and Allah fully knew what she had delivered—“and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”

q: the Mu'mineen, Allaah gives the example of the wife of Fir'oun
(her name was Aasiya bint Mazaahim and she accepted Imaan)
(as Fir'oun was torturing her to death by nailing the hands and feet),
“O my Rabb! Build for me a home by
You in Jannah and save me from Fir'oun, from his actions and save me from the oppressive nation
66:11.s: And God presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people."
66:11.c: And Allah sets forth an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh, who prayed, “My Lord! Build me a house in Paradise near You, deliver me from Pharaoh and his ˹evil˺ doing, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”

q: “You are taking revenge against us merely because we believed in the Aayaat
of our Rabb when it came to us. O our Rabb! Grant us fortitude
and give us death as Muslims
(as people who submit themselves to You).”
7:126.s: And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You]."
7:126.c: Your rage towards us is only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, and let us die while submitting ˹to You˺.”

q: When they went into the battlefield against Jaloot and his army they said, “O our Rabb, pour patience down on us, make our feet firm and help us against the nation of Kaafiroon.”
2:250.s: And when they went forth to [face] Goliath and his soldiers, they said, "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
2:250.c: When they advanced to face Goliath and his warriors, they prayed, “Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, make our steps firm, and give us victory over the disbelieving people.”

q: They said, “We rely on Allaah only. O our Rabb! Do not make us a test for the oppressive ones
(let them not overpower us and therefore think that they are on the right path while we are not).
10:85.s: So they said, "Upon God do we rely. Our Lord, make us not [objects of] trial for the wrongdoing people
10:85.c: They replied, “In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Do not subject us to the persecution of the oppressive people,

q: rescue us with Your mercy from the
those who do not have Imaan.”
10:86.s: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people."
10:86.c: and deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.”

q: (fearing that the king would kill them for believing in Allaah,)
took refuge in the cave saying, “O our Rabb! Bestow on us
a suitable solution to our plight.”
18:10.s: [Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."
18:10.c: ˹Remember˺ when those youths took refuge in the cave, and said, “Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our ordeal.”

q: believed in that which has been revealed to him from his Rabb and
the Mu'mineen. Each one believes in Allaah, His angels, His Books and His Rusul.
“We make no distinction between one and another Messenger
(we believe in every one of them, unlike others like the Jews and the Christians who reject some Prophets),”
our Rabb. To You is our return.”
2:285.s: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination."
2:285.c: The Messenger ˹firmly˺ believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. They ˹all˺ believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers. ˹They proclaim,˺ “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” And they say, “We hear and obey. ˹We seek˺ Your forgiveness, our Lord! And to You ˹alone˺ is the final return.”

q: Allaah does not place on a soul a responsibility
except what is within its capability
(Allaah shall therefore not take one to task for involuntary thoughts that enter one's mind).
which it had earned and to its harm shall be what
“O our Rabb, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes
(do not punish us if we do wrong through forgetfulness or by mistake).
Our Rabb, do not place such responsibilities
on us as You had placed on those before us. Our Rabb, do not enforce
on us that which we do not have the strength to bear. Overlook
forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector so assist us against the nation of Kaafiroon.”
2:286.s: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."
2:286.c: Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford. All good will be for its own benefit, and all evil will be to its own loss. ˹The believers pray,˺ “Our Lord! Do not punish us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord! Do not place a burden on us like the one you placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not burden us with what we cannot bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our ˹only˺ Guardian. So grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”

q: (Those who are sound in knowledge who are not proud and are content with their intellectual achievements and strength of Imaan pray to Allaah saying,)
“Our Rabb, do not cause our hearts to stray after You have guided us. Grant us Your mercy
(O turner of hearts, keep my heart steadfast on your deen)
for verily You are the Great Giver”
3:8.s: [Who say], "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
3:8.c: ˹They say,˺ “Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.

q: “Our Rabb, surely You shall gather mankind together on a day
about which there is no doubt. Surely Allaah never fails to meet an appointment
3:9.s: Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise."
3:9.c: Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the ˹promised˺ Day—about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise.”

q: Those who say, “O our Rabb, we certainly have Imaan
so forgive our sins and save us from the punishment of the fire
3:16.s: Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire,"
3:16.c: who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”

q: was that they would say, “O our Rabb, forgive us our sins and our transgressions
(so that we remain committed to our Creator)
and help us against the nation of Kaafiroon.”
3:147.s: And their words were not but that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess [committed] in our affairs and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
3:147.c: And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”

q: They who remember Allaah while standing, sitting and lying down
(they do not forget Allaah at any time),
and they think about the creation of the heavens and earth
(so that they may be able to see Allaah's greatness in this). (Then, amazed by Allaah's creation, they say)
“Our Rabb You have not created all this without a purpose!
(These things certainly display Your power and greatness and have not been created in vain)
(none can ever be equal to You)
so save us from the punishment of the Fire
3:191.s: Who remember God while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
3:191.c: ˹They are˺ those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth ˹and pray˺, “Our Lord! You have not created ˹all of˺ this without purpose. Glory be to You! Protect us from the torment of the Fire.

q: one whom You enter in the Fire
There shall be none to help the oppressors
3:192.s: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
3:192.c: Our Lord! Indeed, those You commit to the Fire will be ˹completely˺ disgraced! And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.

q: “Our Rabb, we have certainly heard the caller
'Believe in your Rabb!' so we believed. Our Rabb! Pardon our sins, remove from us
(so that no one knows about them)
3:193.s: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller [i.e., Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)] calling to faith, [saying], ‘Believe in your Lord,’ and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.
3:193.c: Our Lord! We have heard the caller to ˹true˺ belief, ˹proclaiming,˺ ‘Believe in your Lord ˹alone˺,’ so we believed. Our Lord! Forgive our sins, absolve us of our misdeeds, and allow us ˹each˺ to die as one of the virtuous.

q: You have promised us through Your Rusul and do not disgrace
us on the Day of Judgement. Verily You do not break Your promise.”
(Although Muslims know well that Allaah never breaks His promises, they pray with these words hoping that Allaah will make them worthy of receiving what He has promised.)
3:194.s: Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise."
3:194.c: Our Lord! Grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not put us to shame on Judgment Day—for certainly You never fail in Your promise.”

q: Those who say, “O our Rabb! Grant us the coolness
(so that they never become a source of regret or distress for us in either world when they follow Islaam properly),
(make our progeny pious and make us pious enough to guide pious people).'
25:74.s: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."
25:74.c: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Bless us with ˹pious˺ spouses and offspring who will be the joy of our hearts, and make us models for the righteous.”

q: (after the Muhaajireen and Ansaar ought to)
say, “O our Rabb! Forgive us and our brothers
who passed before us with Imaan. And do not place any impurity
in our hearts against those who have Imaan. O our Rabb! Indeed You are the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
59:10.s: And [there is a share for] those who came after them, saying, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.”
59:10.c: And those who come after them will pray, “Our Lord! Forgive us and our fellow believers who preceded us in faith, and do not allow bitterness into our hearts towards those who believe. Our Lord! Indeed, You are Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.” The Hypocrites and Banu An-Naḍîr

q: What excuse do you have not to fight in Allaah's way and in defence of the weak men, women and children who
cry out, “O our Rabb! Remove us from this town of oppressors, grant us a defender from Yourself and grant us a helper from Yourself”?
(Jihaad is fought to elevate the Deen and to liberate oppressed Muslims.)
4:75.s: And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of God and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"?
4:75.c: And what is it with you? You do not fight in the cause of Allah and for oppressed men, women, and children who cry out, “Our Lord! Deliver us from this land of oppressors! Appoint for us a saviour; appoint for us a helper—all by Your grace.”

q: Verily those who are present by your Rabb
are not too proud to worship Him. They praise His purity and prostrate to Him
(you should therefore try to be like them). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
7:206.s: Indeed, those who are near your Lord [i.e., the angels] are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate.
7:206.c: Surely those ˹angels˺ nearest to your Lord are not too proud to worship Him. They glorify Him. And to Him they prostrate.

q: To Allaah do all within the heavens and the earth prostrate willingly or unwillingly
(shadows are more prominent during these times). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
13:15.s: And to God prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
13:15.c: To Allah ˹alone˺ bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and the earth—willingly or unwillingly—as do their shadows, morning and evening.

q: fear the authority of their Rabb and do
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
16:50.s: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
16:50.c: They fear their Lord above them, and do whatever they are commanded.

q: (their submission to Allaah). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
17:109.s: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it [i.e., the Qur’ān] increases them in humble submission.
17:109.c: And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.”

q: (Ambiyaa ﵊ mentioned above from Zakariyya ﵊ until Idrees ﵊)
are the ones whom Allaah has favoured from the progeny of Aadam and from the progeny of those whom We carried with Nooh
(some of them such as Ismaa'eel ﵊ and Is'haaq ﵊ were)
from the progeny of Ibraheem and
(others like Moosa ﵊, Haaroon ﵊, Zakariyya ﵊ and were from the progeny of)
those whom We guided and selected. When the Aayaat of their Rabb are recited, they fall down weeping in prostration.
(It is therefore befitting of anyone who reveres them to behave in the same manner.) (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah)
19:58.s: Those were the ones upon whom God bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel [i.e., Jacob], and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
19:58.c: Those were ˹some of˺ the prophets who Allah has blessed from among the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We ˹rightly˺ guided and chose. Whenever the revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to them, they fell down, prostrating and weeping.

q: Do you not see that all within the heavens and the earth prostate
to Allaah, including the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the beasts and many people
(however, man does not perceive the manner in which these creation bow down to Allaah).
And there are many who justly deserve punishment
(because they refuse to submit to Allaah). (When Allaah decides to humiliate a person because of his/her disobedience, no one can help the person because)
the person whom Allaah humiliates. Indeed, Allaah does as He pleases
(and none can challenge His decision). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah)
22:18.s: Do you not see [i.e., know] that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom God humiliates – for him there is no bestower of honour. Indeed, God does what He wills.
22:18.c: Do you not see that to Allah bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and all those on the earth, as well as the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and ˹all˺ living beings, as well as many humans, while many are deserving of punishment. And whoever Allah disgraces, none can honour. Surely Allah does what He wills.

q: O you who have Imaan, bow, prostrate, worship your Rabb and carry out
good deeds so that you may be successful
22:77.s: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.
22:77.c: O believers! Bow down, prostrate yourselves, worship your Lord, and do ˹what is˺ good so that you may be successful.

q: are told, “Prostrate to Ar Rahmaan,” they
“What is Ar Rahmaan? Should we prostrate to whatever you command us?” Their hatred then only increases.
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
25:60.s: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" And it increases them in aversion.
25:60.c: When it is said to them, “Prostrate to the Most Compassionate,” they ask ˹in disgust˺, “What is ‘the Most Compassionate’? Will we prostrate to whatever you order us to?” And it only drives them farther away.

q: “Allaah is the One besides Whom there is no other Ilaah. He is the Rabb of the glorious throne
(which is far superior to any throne of this world).” (One who recites or hears this verse being recited must perform Sajdah.)
27:26.s: God - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne."
27:26.c: ˹He is˺ Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”

32:15.s: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
32:15.c: The only ˹true˺ believers in Our revelation are those who—when it is recited to them—fall into prostration and glorify the praises of their Lord and are not too proud.

q: said, “He has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes. Indeed, there are many partners who transgress against each other, except for those who have Imaan and who do righteous deeds.
It occurred to Dawood ﵊ that We had tested him
(by presenting to him a case that appeared to be straightforward and which came from people who displayed great disrespect, causing him to neglect listening to both sides),
so he sought forgiveness from his Rabb, fell prostrate, and turned to Him in repentance.
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
38:24.s: [David] said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to God].
38:24.c: David ˹eventually˺ ruled, “He has definitely wronged you in demanding ˹to add˺ your sheep to his. And certainly many partners wrong each other, except those who believe and do good—but how few are they!” Then David realized that We had tested him so he asked for his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned ˹to Him in repentance˺.

q: (Allaah does not need their worship because)
who are close to your Rabb glorify Him day and night without becoming tired.
(One who recite or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
41:38.s: But if they are arrogant - then those who are near your Lord [i.e., the angels] exalt Him by night and by day, and they do not become weary.
41:38.c: But if the pagans are too proud, then ˹let them know that˺ those ˹angels˺ nearest to your Lord glorify Him day and night, and never grow weary.

q: Prostrate to Allaah and worship Him
(if you are wise). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
53:62.s: So prostrate to God and worship [Him].
53:62.c: Instead, prostrate to Allah and worship ˹Him alone˺!

q: ...and do not prostrate when the Qur'aan is recited to them?
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
84:21.s: And when the Qur’ān is recited to them, they do not prostrate [to God]?
84:21.c: and when the Quran is recited to them, they do not bow down ˹in submission˺?

q: (in the future just as you had never done in the past)!
(performing salaah without being intimidated by anyone)
(to Allaah). (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah).
96:19.s: No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to God].
96:19.c: Again, no! Never obey him ˹O Prophet˺! Rather, ˹continue to˺ prostrate and draw near ˹to Allah˺.
